'''Hossam Haick''' ({{langx|ar|حسام حايك}}; {{langx|he|חוסאם חאיק}}; {{IPAc-en|h|aɪ|k}} {{Respell|HYKE}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjq8-AeiLLE|title=Nanotechnology and Nanosensors with Hossam Haick|work=YouTube|date=5 October 2014|accessdate=16 November 2021}}</ref> born 1975)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.jpost.com/magazine/young-israelis-of-the-year-dr-hossam-haick-34-sniffing-out-cancer-155433 | title=Young Israelis of the year: Dr. Hossam Haick, 34: Sniffing out cancer | date=18 September 2009 }}</ref> is an Arab-Israeli scientist and engineer, who is a Full Professor at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]]. He is known for his research in nanotechnology and non-invasive disease diagnostics, particularly for developing artificially intelligent sensory technologies, including the Nano Artificial Nose (NA-NOSE) and the A-Patch. These platforms are designed to detect disease-related biomarkers from non-invasive biological sources, including exhaled breath and the skin.<ref name=":1">{{cite web | url=https://www.haaretz.com/weekend/week-s-end/the-israeli-scientist-who-is-sniffing-out-cancer-1.299656 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021145109/http://www.haaretz.com/weekend/week-s-end/the-israeli-scientist-who-is-sniffing-out-cancer-1.299656 | url-status=dead | archive-date=21 October 2013 | title=The Israeli scientist who is sniffing out cancer | work=Haaretz | date=2 July 2010 | accessdate=25 January 2015 | author=Grimland, Guy}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2016/02/23/world/middleeast/ap-ml-israel-arab-academic.html | title=Arab Professor Breaks Barriers at Home and Abroad | work=[[The New York Times]]| date=23 February 2016 | accessdate= | author=}}</ref>

In 2026, Haick was awarded the Israeli Presidential Medal of Honour and became a Fellow of the United States National Academy of Inventors.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Fruit flies give further insight into evolution of male genitalia driven by sexual selection |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1032943 |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=www.eurekalert.org}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Hossam Haick Elected Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors |url=https://technionuk.org/news-post/prof-hossam-haick-elected-fellow-of-the-national-academy-of-inventors/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Technion UK |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Israeli Presidential Medal of Honour Awarded to Technion's Prof. Hossam Haick |url=https://www.technion.ac.il/en/blog/article/israeli-presidential-medal-of-honour-awarded-to-technions-prof-hossam-haick/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=הטכניון-מכון טכנולוגי לישראל |language=en-US}}</ref> He has published more than 500 scientific publications and holds more than 100 patents, many of which have been licensed to international companies.<ref name=":5" /> His work has received more than 37,000 citations on Google Scholar, with an h-index of 100.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Hossam Haick |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=pZtQQ-sAAAAJ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

His research has been supported by major competitive grants and awards, including the Marie Curie Excellence Grant, grants from the European Research Council (ERC), and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Awards.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Hossam Haick |url=https://www.technioncanada.org/our-team/hossam-haick/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Technion |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Hossam Haick |url=https://ats.org/about/faces-of-the-technion/hossam-haick/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=American Technion Society |language=en-US}}</ref> He was appointed a Knight of the Order of Academic Palms by the French government in 2010 and was included in the GOOD 100 list of global citizens and creative change-makers from 2015 to 2018 and 35 Top Young Inventors (TR35) by MIT Technology Review as well as in additional >90 international scientific rankings, including Stanford University's list of the world's top 2% most-cited scientists from 2021 to 2026.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Faces behind EuroTech: Hossam Haick, Technion |url=https://eurotech-universities.eu/news-and-events/news/faces-behind-eurotech-hossam-haick-technion/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=EuroTech Universities Alliance |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Professor Hossam Haick is included in GOOD Magazine's 2016 "GOOD 100" |url=https://lnbd.technion.ac.il/news/professor-hossam-haick-included-good-magazines-2016-good-100/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=LNBD |language=en-US}}</ref>  He served as Dean of the School of Undergraduate Studies at the Technion from 2020 to 2026.<ref name=":7" />

== Early life and education ==
Haick was born in 1975 in [[Nazareth|Nazareth, Israel]], into an [[Arab Christian]] family.<ref>[https://www.jpost.com/Magazine/Young-Israelis-of-the-year-Dr-Hossam-Haick-34-Sniffing-out-cancer Young Israelis of the year: Dr. Hossam Haick, 34: Sniffing out cancer]</ref> He attended St. Joseph Seminary and High School in Nazareth.<ref name=":6" /> He received his B.Sc. in Chemical Engineering from Ben-Gurion University in 1998,<ref name=":6" /> and his Ph.D. from the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology in 2002.<ref name=":8" /> He completed postdoctoral fellowships at the Weizmann Institute of Science (2002–2004) and at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) (2004–2006).

==Career==
Haick joined the Technion faculty in 2006 as an Assistant Professor in the Wolfson Faculty of Chemical Engineering.<ref name=":6" /> He was promoted to Associate Professor with tenure in 2010, and to Full Professor in 2013 in Chemical Engineering.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":7" /> From 2007 to 2011, he headed the Marie-Curie Excellence Centre for Nanomaterial-Based Artificial Olfactory Systems at the Technion. He received a secondary appointment as Full Professor in Biomedical Engineering in 2019.<ref name=":8" /> He served as Dean of the School of Undergraduate Studies from 2020 to 2026.<ref name=":7" /> He held visiting positions as Guest Professor at Ningbo University in China (2017–2020), Visiting Professor at the Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research in Mainz (2016–2017), and Co-director of the International Associated Laboratory between INSERM, Université Paris-Sud, and the Technion (2013–2022).<ref name=":8" />

Haick has founded and coordinated multiple major European research consortia. He founded and coordinated VOLGACORE under the ERA-NET EuroNanoMed-II programme (2013–2017), focused on volatile biomarkers for early detection and characterisation of gastric and colorectal neoplasms.<ref name=":8" /> He founded and coordinated the LCAOS consortium under the EU's FP7 Health programme (2011–2015). He founded and coordinated the SniffPhone project, an EU Horizon 2020 initiative (2015–2019) that developed a smartphone-attachable device for non-invasive breath-based disease detection, partnering with institutions across five countries.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=ben-oz |first=shlomi |date=2018-11-26 |title=European Innovation Prize to Prof. Haick |url=https://www.technion.ac.il/en/blog/2018/11/european-innovation-prize-to-prof-haick/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=הטכניון-מכון טכנולוגי לישראל |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":11">{{Cite web |title=Shaping Europe's digital future |url=https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/page-not-found |access-date= |website=digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu |language=en}}</ref> In 2018, SniffPhone received the European Commission Innovation Prize at EFECS in Lisbon.<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":11" /> He also founded and coordinated VOGAS under the EU's Horizon 2020 CELAC programme (2019–2023), and the A-Patch consortium, also under EU Horizon 2020 (2019–2023), developing wearable sensing patches for infectious disease detection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Screening of Gastric Cancer via Breath volatile organic compounds by Hybrid Sensing Approach {{!}} VOGAS {{!}} Project {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} H2020 |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/824986 |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-29 |title=The project A-PATCH has been finished |url=https://www.kpmi.lu.lv/jaunumi/zinas/zina/t/80913 |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=www.kpmi.lu.lv |language=lv}}</ref> In 2023, he founded and began coordinating the LUCIA consortium under Horizon Europe's EU Cancer Mission. Since 2025, he has founded and coordinated VOLABIOS, a Horizon Europe Health Programme consortium. His most recent consortium, CLARITY-PD, assembles an international consortium of 28 partnering entities from six EU countries and three associated countries to advance non-invasive diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. In total, he has founded and coordinated eight EU consortia, each comprising 17–42 partners from academia, industry, and the public sector, and has served as a core partner in five additional EU consortia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nature |first=Research Communities by Springer |title=Hossam Haick |url=https://communities.springernature.com/users/46166-hossam-haick |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Research Communities by Springer Nature |language=en}}</ref>

Haick is a co-founder of five companies that emerged from academic research,<ref name=":5" /> including Nanose Medical Ltd, where he has served as Co-founder and Chief Scientific Officer since 2019;<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://nanosemed.com/about/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Nanose |language=en-US}}</ref> and FeelIT Ltd, where he has been Co-founder since 2017.<ref name=":8" />

== Research ==
Haick's research focuses on the development of nanosensor-based artificial sensing systems for the non-invasive and minimally invasive detection and diagnosis of disease. His work explores disease-related biomarkers from a wide range of biological sources, including exhaled breath, skin, blood, body fluids, and tissue samples, with particular emphasis on extracting diagnostic information without the need for conventional invasive procedures. His group developed the Nano Artificial Nose (NA-NOSE), a nanomaterial-based sensing platform designed to identify disease-specific molecular signatures and enable the detection of conditions such as cancer, Parkinson's disease, and other disorders.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":6" /> His 2009 paper in ''Nature Nanotechnology'' demonstrated the diagnosis of lung cancer from exhaled breath using gold-nanoparticle sensor arrays and helped establish the concept of breath-based disease detection.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Peng |first1=Gang |last2=Tisch |first2=Ulrike |last3=Adams |first3=Orna |last4=Hakim |first4=Meggie |last5=Shehada |first5=Nisrean |last6=Broza |first6=Yoav Y. |last7=Billan |first7=Salem |last8=Abdah-Bortnyak |first8=Roxolyana |last9=Kuten |first9=Abraham |last10=Haick |first10=Hossam |date=2009 |title=Diagnosing lung cancer in exhaled breath using gold nanoparticles |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nnano.2009.235 |journal=Nature Nanotechnology |language=en |volume=4 |issue=10 |pages=669–673 |doi=10.1038/nnano.2009.235 |pmid=19809459 |bibcode=2009NatNa...4..669P |issn=1748-3387|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In subsequent large-scale clinical studies, his group provided evidence that different diseases generate distinct and characteristic patterns – or “fingerprints” – of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath. The demonstration of disease-specific volatile fingerprints across 17 different diseases represented a major milestone in the development of volatilomics and provided a foundation for using volatile molecular patterns for non-invasive disease detection and classification.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nakhleh |first1=Morad K. |last2=Amal |first2=Haitham |last3=Jeries |first3=Raneen |last4=Broza |first4=Yoav Y. |last5=Aboud |first5=Manal |last6=Gharra |first6=Alaa |last7=Ivgi |first7=Hodaya |last8=Khatib |first8=Salam |last9=Badarneh |first9=Shifaa |last10=Har-Shai |first10=Lior |last11=Glass-Marmor |first11=Lea |last12=Lejbkowicz |first12=Izabella |last13=Miller |first13=Ariel |last14=Badarny |first14=Samih |last15=Winer |first15=Raz |date=2017-01-24 |title=Diagnosis and Classification of 17 Diseases from 1404 Subjects via Pattern Analysis of Exhaled Molecules |journal=ACS Nano |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=112–125 |doi=10.1021/acsnano.6b04930 |issn=1936-086X |pmc=5269643 |pmid=28000444 |bibcode=2017ACSNa..11..112N }}</ref>

== Publications and patents ==
Haick has published more than 500 scientific publications in top-level journals across his career, including more than 300 in the past decade, in the fields of nanotechnology, advanced materials, chemistry, and medicine. He has edited two books and more than ten book chapters. His work has been cited more than 37,000 times on Google Scholar, with an h-index of 100.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":12" /> In 2022, he edited ''Volatile Biomarkers for Human Health: From Nature to Artificial Senses'', published by the Royal Society of Chemistry, which examines volatile biomarkers and their use in artificial sensing systems for health-related applications.<ref name=":13">{{Cite book |url=https://books.rsc.org/books/edited-volume/2024/Volatile-Biomarkers-for-Human-HealthFrom-Nature-to |title=Volatile Biomarkers for Human Health: From Nature to Artificial Senses |date=2022-09-30 |publisher=The Royal Society of Chemistry |isbn=978-1-83916-430-9 |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, he edited ''Nature-Inspired Sensors'', published by Elsevier, which addresses sensing technologies and concepts inspired by biological and natural systems.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |title=Nature Inspired Sensors |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/book/edited-volume/9780443156847/nature-inspired-sensors}}</ref>
